subject: Pricing options for BlueGrid - per-token commit & exception request
messages:
From: Anna Reyes <anna@bluegrid.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Inquiry on committed tier pricing and potential exception

Hi Sean / Dev,

Thanks for the chat earlier. BlueGrid is looking at high-volume usage for Q2 and beyond — we expect a steady run rate of ~1.1M tokens/month initially, trending toward 1.6M in six months as we onboard two product lines.

Two asks from procurement: 1) confirmation of per-token rate card for hosted API (standard list) and 2) whether Redwood can offer a custom committed tier with a steeper discount (we were hoping ~25% off list) in exchange for a 12-month commit.

Can you send options for: a) pay-as-you-go rate-card pricing, b) 12-month commit/volume tiers with blended per-token pricing, and c) what internal approvals would be required for a discount >20%?

Also copying procurement@bluegrid.com for formal procurement steps.

Thanks,
Anna Reyes\Senior Procurement Manager\BlueGrid Systems

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anna Reyes <anna@bluegrid.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry on committed tier pricing and potential exception

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short options spreadsheet with two paths that would meet your use case. Summary below.

Option A — Rate-card / standard tiers (no special approval)
- List (pay-as-you-go): $0.0008 per token (hosted API list)
- Committed tier 800k+/mo: 15% off list
- No additional approvals required; standard SLA and T&Cs apply

Option B — Custom commit (requires pricing exception approval)
- Proposed: 1.2M tokens/mo commit for 12 months
- Blended effective rate: $0.00064 per token (20% off list) as baseline
- If customer requests 25% off, that exceeds our threshold and needs Sales Ops + VP sign-off and Finance review for margin impact

Attachments: BlueGrid_pricing_options.xlsx (breakdown + modeled spend)

Next steps: if Option B looks interesting, I can request an internal exception and escalate with the deal summary + expected revenue. Otherwise we can proceed with Option A and finalize via our standard procurement flow.

Would love to jump on a 30-min procurement/deal-ops call this week if that helps.

Best,
Sean Gallagher\Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BlueGrid pricing options — recommended escalation path

Sean — quick internal note.

- Any discount request >20% requires Sales Ops validation and VP approval per our pricing policy. We also need Finance to sign off on the revenue recognition and commit terms (esp. breakage assumptions).
- If BlueGrid pushes for 25%, the ask will almost certainly need a documented exception (ticket) and a backup plan (shorter initial term or milestone-based increases).

Recommendation: propose a provisional 20% off list for first 6 months tied to a 12-month commit at 1.2M tokens/mo, with a Q2 review and an automatic step-down to 10% thereafter if usage targets are met/not met. This keeps margin dilution limited while giving the customer their desired economics up front.

If you want me to open the exception ticket I can do that (I’ll need the modeled ARR, expected monthly invoices, and the HubSpot link).

Thanks,
Dev Patel\Sales Operations
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BlueGrid pricing options — request for pricing exception approval

Forwarding summary for approval:

- Account: BlueGrid Systems (deal_BG_8421)
- Customer ask: 25% off list in exchange for 12-month commit (projected 1.2–1.6M tokens/mo)
- Our preliminary offer: 20% off list for first 6 months with 12-month commit at 1.2M tokens/mo; review after 6 months
- Impact: estimated blended ARR reduction vs list ~22% for first 6 months; modeled ARR and margin in Drive (link below)

Requesting: VP approval to issue a one-time pricing exception (20% for six months) and permission for Sales Ops to create the exception ticket and route to Finance/Legal. If approved, Sean will share the MoU (DocuSign) and we’ll request Procurement to sign.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bBlueGridPricing
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/8421

Marissa\Director, Sales\Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueGrid pricing options — request for pricing exception approval

Marissa / team — I reviewed the summary and the modeled impact. Approve a provisional pricing exception with the following guardrails:

1) Approve 20% off list for first 6 months, contingent on signed 12-month MoU with a minimum commit of 1.2M tokens/month.
2) After month 6, automatic review to move price to 10% off list for the remainder of the term unless usage materially exceeds projections (in which case Sales and Finance will revisit).
3) Finance must sign the MoU (revenue recognition check) and Legal must include an early-termination clause and overage pricing in the SOW.

Sales Ops: please generate discount_exception_ticket_8742.pdf and route to Finance. Sean, once you have the signed MoU, loop Legal and Billing to put the customer onto Dedicated billing terms.

-Laura
Laura Bennett\VP, Sales
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anna Reyes <anna@bluegrid.com>
Cc: procurement@bluegrid.com, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Approved: BlueGrid provisional pricing exception & next steps

Anna — good news: leadership has approved a provisional exception per the terms below. (See Laura’s note quoted after.)

Summary of approved terms:
- Discount: 20% off hosted API list price for tokens
- Commit: 1.2M tokens/month minimum, 12-month term
- Initial period: 20% for first 6 months, then automatic review to step down to 10% unless usage exceeds targets
- Required: signed MoU and Finance sign-off prior to activation

Next steps for BlueGrid:
1) Please review and sign the MoU (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/exec?doc=BG-MoU-202603).
2) Procurement to confirm billing contact and PO cadence (procurement@bluegrid.com).
3) I’ll coordinate Legal and Billing to add contract language for early termination and overage pricing.

Attached: MoU_BlueGrid_March2026.pdf (draft) and the exception ticket (discount_exception_ticket_8742.pdf).

Quotation from Laura Bennett (VP Sales):
> Marissa / team — I reviewed the summary and the modeled impact. Approve a provisional pricing exception with the following guardrails:
>
> 1) Approve 20% off list for first 6 months, contingent on signed 12-month MoU with a minimum commit of 1.2M tokens/month.
> 2) After month 6, automatic review to move price to 10% off list for the remainder of the term unless usage materially exceeds projections (in which case Sales and Finance will revisit).
> 3) Finance must sign the MoU (revenue recognition check) and Legal must include an early-termination clause and overage pricing in the SOW.

Happy to set up a procurement call this week to walk through the MoU and timeline.

Best,
Sean Gallagher\Account Executive, Redwood Inference
